tromerosaurus:table:1.title: 2026 in archosaur paleontology (table of new taxa)

tromerosaurus:study:1.title: A new albertosaurine from the Oldman Formation, Alberta, Canada, illuminates ambiguity between albertosaurine and tyrannosaurine characteristics (Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, 2026)

facts.statement: Stuart Plotkin discovered the holotype skeleton of Tromerosaurus in 2010 in the upper Oldman Formation in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: In 2010, Stuart Plotkin discovered the remains of a tyrannosaur skeleton in outcrops of the upper Oldman Formation (quarry Q258) in eastern Dinosaur Provincial Park in Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: Tromerosaurus lived during the Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous in Canada.
facts.quote: Tromerosaurus () is an extinct genus of tyrannosaurid theropod dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian age) of Canada.

facts.statement: The holotype maxillae bear 13 teeth, while the referred specimen TMP 1994.012.0602 has 15 teeth.
facts.quote: The maxillae of the T. solumons holotype bear 13 teeth, in contrast to the 15 teeth in the referred specimen TMP 1994.012.0602.

facts.statement: Tromerosaurus is classified within the subfamily Albertosaurinae, though it shares some features with tyrannosaurines.
facts.quote: A placement within the subfamily Albertosaurinae is preferred, though some anatomical features of Tromerosaurus are reminiscent of tyrannosaurines.

facts.statement: Parsimony analyses recovered Tromerosaurus as the most basal member of the subfamily Albertosaurinae.
facts.quote: In all versions of their parsimony analyses, Tromerosaurus was recovered as the basalmost member of the tyrannosaurid subfamily Albertosaurinae, which also includes Albertosaurus and Gorgosaurus.

facts.statement: Bayesian analyses by Powers et al. (2026) placed Tromerosaurus as the most basal member of the subfamily Tyrannosaurinae, conflicting with parsimony results.
facts.quote: In contrast to their parsimony results, the Bayesian results of Powers et al. (2026) placed Tromerosaurus as the basalmost member of the subfamily Tyrannosaurinae (the sister group to Albertosaurinae).

facts.statement: The conflicting phylogenetic results highlight a mosaic anatomy in Tromerosaurus, featuring traits of both albertosaurines and early tyrannosaurines.
facts.quote: While the albertosaurine placement was preferred, these conflicting results highlight the mosaic anatomy of Tromerosaurus, with some features similar to both albertosaurines and early tyrannosaurines.

facts.statement: Two isolated maxillae from unknown localities were tentatively referred to the species, representing a mature individual and a small juvenile.
facts.quote: Two isolated maxillae (primary upper tooth-bearing bones) from unknown localities were tentatively also referred, one of which (UALVP 56605) belongs to a mature individual, while the other (TMP 1985.011.0003) belongs to a small juvenile.

facts.statement: Stuart Plotkin discovered tyrannosaurid remains in the upper zone of the Oldman Formation near the Provincial Dinosaur Park in Alberta, Canada, in 2010.
facts.quote: En 2010, Stuart Plotkin descubrió los restos de un esqueleto de tiranosáurido en los afloramientos de la zona superior de la Formación Oldman (cantera Q258) al este del Parque provincial de los Dinosaurios en Alberta, Canadá.

facts.statement: A team from the University of Alberta assisted in the excavation of the specimen between 2010 and 2011.
facts.quote: Un equipo de la Universidad de Alberta (UA) asistió en la excavación del espécimen entre 2010 a 2011.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is cataloged as UALVP 52981 and is housed at the University of Alberta's Vertebrate Paleontology Laboratory.
facts.quote: Dicho ejemplar está alojado en el Laboratorio de Paleontología de Vertebrados de la UA (UALVP), en donde está catalogado como el espécimen UALVP 52981.

facts.statement: Mark J. Powers and colleagues described Tromerosaurus solumons as a new tyrannosaurid genus and species in 2026, designating UALVP 52981 as the holotype.
facts.quote: En 2026, Mark J. Powers y colaboradores describieron a Tromerosaurus solumons como un nuevo género y especie de terópodo tiranosáurido con base en estos restos fósiles, designando a UALVP 52981 como el ejemplar holotipo.

facts.statement: Specimens TMP 1994.012.0602 and TMP 1995.005.0001 were referred to Tromerosaurus solumons based on shared anatomical characteristics with the holotype.
facts.quote: TMP 1994.012.0602 y TMP 1995.005.0001 fueron referidos a esta especie con base en las características anatómicas compartidas con el holotipo.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of an incomplete but articulated skeleton including most of the skull and most of the postcranium, such as neck and trunk vertebrae, gastralia, ribs, both humeri, the pelvis, and most of the right leg.
facts.quote: Consiste de un esqueleto incompleto aunque articulado que incluye la mayor parte del cráneo (faltándole los espleniales y algunos componentes del lado derecho) y la mayor parte del postcráneo (con vértebras del cuello y tronco, la gastralia, costillas, ambos húmeros, la pelvis y la mayor parte de la pata derecha).

facts.statement: Digital reconstruction suggests the skull of the holotype is up to 90 centimeters long.
facts.quote: Al ser reconstruido digitalmente, su longitud sería de hasta 90 centímetros.

facts.statement: The femur of the holotype measures 95 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El fémur es más largo, con 95 cm.

facts.statement: The snout accounts for more than 60% of the skull length, which maintains a relatively consistent height from the snout to the back of the skull.
facts.quote: El hocico abarca más del 60% de la longitud del cráneo, el cual mantiene altura mayormente consistente desde el hocico hasta la parte posterior del cráneo.

facts.statement: The holotype of T. solumons possesses 13 maxillary teeth, contrasting with 15 teeth in the referred specimen TMP 1994.012.0602.
facts.quote: Los maxilares del holotipo de T. solumons poseen 13 dientes, en contraste con los 15 dientes en el espécimen referido TMP 1994.012.0602.

facts.statement: The dentary of the holotype has 16 teeth, falling within the range of 15 to 18 seen in Gorgosaurus.
facts.quote: El dentario tiene 16 dientes, dentro del rango de los 15–18 vistos en Gorgosaurus.

facts.statement: In all most parsimonious versions of their analyses, Powers et al. recovered Tromerosaurus as the most basal member of the subfamily Albertosaurinae, which also includes Albertosaurus and Gorgosaurus.
facts.quote: En todas las versiones de sus análisis más parsimoniosos, Tromerosaurus fue recuperado como el miembro más basal de la subfamilia de tiranosaúridos Albertosaurinae, la cual incluye también a Albertosaurus y Gorgosaurus.

facts.statement: In contrast to their parsimony results, the Bayesian analysis by Powers et al. (2026) placed Tromerosaurus as the most basal member of the subfamily Tyrannosaurinae, the sister group to Albertosaurinae.
facts.quote: En contraste con sus resultados por parsimonia, los resultados de análisis bayesiano de Powers et al. (2026) situaron a Tromerosaurus como el miembro más basal de la subfamilia Tyrannosaurinae (el grupo hermano de los Albertosaurinae).

facts.statement: While the Albertosaurinae classification was preferred, contradictory results highlight the mosaic anatomy of Tromerosaurus, possessing traits similar to both albertosaurines and early tyrannosaurines.
facts.quote: Si bien se prefirió la clasificación dentro de los albertosaurinos, estos resultados contradictorios resaltan la anatomía de mosaico de Tromerosaurus, con algunos rasgos parecidos tanto a los albertosaurinos como a los primeros tiranosaurinos.

facts.statement: Two isolated maxillae from unknown deposits were tentatively referred to the species: UALVP 56605 from a mature individual and TMP 1985.011.0003 from a small juvenile.
facts.quote: También se refirieron tentativamente a dos maxilares aislados (los huesos que sostienen a la mayoría de los dientes superiores) de yacimientos desconocidos, uno de los cuales (UALVP 56605) pertenece a un individuo maduro, mientras que el otro (TMP 1985.011.0003) pertenece a un juvenil pequeño.

facts.statement: The genus name Tromerosaurus combines the Ancient Greek words tromerós, meaning "terrible" or "frightening", and saûros, meaning "lizard".
facts.quote: El nombre del género, Tromerosaurus, combina las palabras del griego antiguo τρομερός (tromerós), que significa "terrible" o "aterrador", y σαῦρος (saûros), que significa "lagarto".

facts.statement: The species name solumons derives from the Latin words solus, meaning "solitary", and mōns, meaning "mountain".
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, solumons, se deriva de las palabras en latín solus, que significa "solitario" y mōns, que se traduce como "montaña".
